This page from the Pew Research Center presents data on public satisfaction with the state of the nation in January 2019. It highlights that 70% of Americans are dissatisfied, a 9-point increase since September 2018, while only 26% are satisfied. The data shows a significant decline in Republican satisfaction, which has dropped to 47%, the lowest level since late 2017, and a record low of 8% among Democrats. The page includes two line charts: one showing the long-term trend of national satisfaction from 1990 to 2019, and another comparing satisfaction levels by political affiliation during different presidential administrations.

**Text Evidence:**
- 70% of Americans are dissatisfied with the way things are going in the country.
- Only 26% of adults say they are satisfied with the state of the nation.
- Public dissatisfaction has increased by 9 percentage points since September 2018 (from 61%).
- Among Republicans, 47% are dissatisfied and 47% are satisfied, a 12-percentage-point drop in satisfaction from September.
- Just 8% of Democrats are satisfied, while 90% are dissatisfied.
- Democratic satisfaction has dropped modestly from 14% in September but has never exceeded 16% during Trump's presidency.

**Visual Evidence:**

In 2019, under President Trump, Republican satisfaction was 47% and Democratic satisfaction was 8%.</chart_summary>
